result:
The FLOP count is 2·M·N·K = 2 × 256 × 18560 × 4096 ≈ 38.9 GFLOP.

With M=256 the GEMM is a skinny one. Arithmetic intensity is not the limit, but wave quantization and tile shape are. Memory traffic is the B matrix (18560×4096×2 B ≈ 152 MB) plus A (about 2 MB) and C (about 9.5 MB), so roughly 164 MB. At about 7 TB/s of HBM3e bandwidth on a B300 that is about 23 µs. Compute at a realistic dense BF16 rate of ~2.0–2.3 PFLOPS is about 17–20 µs. The two are close, so the kernel is near memory-bound and lands around 30 µs after accounting for achievable bandwidth (~80%), tile quantization, and launch/tail effects within a CUDA graph.

I did not run this, so it is an estimate rather than a measurement.
